main_text.p: obstaculo fint, eruendos, Matth. 5. Eccles. 9. Prouerb. 5. & pedes amputandos, ne aduran-tur igne gehennae.

ȝ[?] Praeterea grauitas adulterij, & mala quae inde oriuntur expendamus. Periculosius est & detrimentosius atque peius est adulte-rare, quàm furari (quod hodie pauci credunt, id quod ex supplicijs furum & adulterorum intelligitur) adhaec scortatio, mala animae, corporis, famae & fortunae importat. vt ex Luc. 15. etiam cognoscere licet, nec non ex Germanico illo prouerbio: Spiel/ Hu-rey / vnd sauffen / macht daß ich muß haben vnd gut verkauffen : oder / von hauß vnnd hoff lauffen.

Attenuatur[?] autem hic peccatum furti non simpliciter, pro quo grauis poena infligitur secundum legem, sed temporalis & citra mortem, vt scilicet reddat septuplum, id est, plura quàm abstulit indeterminatè, boues quinque pro vno, oues quatuor pro vna, Exod.22. vel totum quod habet: sed comparatione adulterij longè grauioris, Is enim adulter remedium vxoris habet & matrimonij, vel habere debet, qua incontinentiae medeatur. Fur vero necessitate compulsus, nempe famis iniuriam euadere cupiens, deprehensus vero satisfacit, minori confusioni obnoxius postea, quàm illi, qui necessitatem patienti non succurrerunt, in ius traxerunt, spoliaverunt bonis pauperem, qui non vt ditesceret, sed vt esurientem stomachum placaret & impleret,

page.notes: The first line opens mid-sentence from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The paragraph sign before "Praeterea" is a printed ornament that is hard to read; marked [?]. "Attenuatur" and "poena" are doubtful in the scan (the letters look like "Atrenuatur" and "prœna"); marked [?]. The German black letter is set inside roman text and is marked bl. The last word of the page is printed "impleret," with the break marked by an unprinted hyphen, so it is written whole. A printed dot at the lower right and marks at the left edge are not text and are left out.
